slides.title: AI Updates Codebase Memory MCP A fast and
slides.text: AI Updates Codebase Memory MCP A fast and token efficient MCP server that indexes codebases into a persistent knowledge graph for AI coding agents https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp It parses source code with tree-sitter and stores structural relationships like functions, classes, calls, imports, and routes locally in SQLite https://www.tecmint.com/install-codebase-memory-mcp-linux/ Agents query the graph instead of rereading files, which can cut token usage dramatically Reported performance is very high, with average repos indexed in milliseconds and structural queries answered in under 1 ms It is open source, ships as a single static binary with zero dependencies, and works across major desktop operating systems https://skillsllm.com/skill/codebase-memory-mcp https://codebase-memory.com Thinking Machines Inkling-Small 276B Open-weight, multimodal, x4 smaller, nearly same performance Context length 1M tokens API pricing starting at $0.58 per 1M input tokens https://thinkingmachines.ai/news/inkling-small/ Demis Hassabis is stepping down as Google DeepMind CEO and moving into a chairman role, while also becoming Chief Scientist of Alphabet Day‑to‑day leadership of Google DeepMind shifts to Koray Kavukcuoglu as senior VP reporting to Sundar Pichai.

slides.title: AI Updates Muse Code vs Claude Code curl
slides.text: AI Updates Muse Code vs Claude Code curl -fsSL https://dev.meta.ai/install.sh | bash https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gjw3ok6alYY https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2 Muse Code is Meta’s new terminal-based AI coding agent, built as a harness around the Muse Spark 1.2 model, focused on long-horizon software engineering and large repos Harness features: Automatic fan-out to parallel subagents with isolated project copies, append-only local event log with crash-resume, and bundled skills like /plan, /grill, and /goal for planning and interrogation Positioning vs Claude Code: Weaker frontier-level brain than top models like Claude, but a strong, transparent harness aimed at being a cheap, fast sub-agent inside multi-model systems rather than a primary builder Muse Spark 1.2: 1M-token context coding model, “fast, cheap worker”, co-trained inside Muse Code optimized for long debugging sessions, multi-file changes, and persistent tool use /doctor is a built‑in Claude Code command It runs health checks on your installation, configuration, skills, MCP servers, Claude.md, and token-heavy context, then reports what’s healthy, what’s misconfigured, and what you can safely trim or fix You just type /doctor (or run “claude doctor”) and it updates with Claude Code itself.

slides.title: Five Layers of AI Operating System Agent OS
slides.text: Five Layers of AI Operating System Agent OS - by Julian Goldie SEO Agent Operating System is a unified “ mission control ” where multiple AI agents (builder, designer, video, SEO, music) collaborate with shared memory and custom workflows Models are swappable (Hermes, Claude, GPT variants, local LFM2.5–2.6B), letting you trade speed, cost, and rate limits Runs on modest hardware (laptop is OK) Includes loop and goal modes Lets you easily plug new models, tools, and workflows Google Search Console integration (now with social data) drives automated SEO content creation from ranking keywords. Fast 20-30 min local setup Layer 1 - Mission-Control Dashboard - AI models and Agents Layer 2 - Memory (obsidian wiki) - bus. context, prefs, logs Layer 3 - Router - router tasks - saves money Layer 4 - Agents (Workers & Workflows) - parallel worker agents that carry out specific tasks using systems like a Kanban board and controlled by a single commander agent Layer 5 - Loop Engineering (Continuous Improvement) - updates the memory, making future outputs smarter https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3OZiTbD1OU https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZhJi_npUQcQ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ru07BOhF1wk https://buzz.xyz Hermes Agent + Buzz team workspace https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/buzz https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b42vjtH6mNM Hermes Agent + Buzz team workspace https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/buzz https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b42vjtH6mNM Hermes Agent 0.20 This is the "Herald" release (finding its voice) Adds real-time voice. It can speak while thinking, accept interruptions, wake on a custom wake word Voice notes now work across apps like WhatsApp Grounded citations, safer approval prompts, faster responses, better compression, and agent-to-agent coordination “Open line” idea - continuous collaboration

slides.title: AI Updates Tencent Open-Source AI Memory System https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5AkurBDSYwo
slides.text: AI Updates Tencent Open-Source AI Memory System https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5AkurBDSYwo Large context windows degrade LLM performance over time, causing AI agents to waste tokens and repeat previous mistakes Tencent released an open-source MIT-licensed memory plugin designed to cut token overhead while drastically boosting benchmark success rates The framework compresses raw execution logs into interactive Mermaid diagrams while keeping detailed underlying evidence stored safely on disk Inspired by cognitive psychology, it structures memory into episodic events and four semantic layers, ranging from facts to persona defaults Running locally via SQLite, it provides fast hybrid search, complete privacy, and zero API vendor dependencies for long-running workflows. GraphRAG - Better than Vectors https://github.com/microsoft/graphrag https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yqEekIQSVzQ https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/from-local-to-global-graph-rag/ RAG shifts retrieval from flat chunks to entities and typed links Microsoft’s GraphRAG showed better multi-document answers, but early builds were expensive Lazy GraphRAG cut indexing cost dramatically by moving work to query time Stanford and Anthropic highlighted extractor quality, entity resolution, and chain-of-facts limits The main lesson is to use graphs when questions depend on relationships, not simple lookup

slides.title: AI Updates ZLUDA: Running CUDA on AMD Graphics
slides.text: AI Updates ZLUDA: Running CUDA on AMD Graphics https://github.com/vosen/ZLUDA https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TRoOflwNagg ZLUDA is an open-source software compatibility layer that allows unmodified NVIDIA CUDA applications to run directly on AMD Radeon GPUs It translates PTX instructions on the fly, enabling local AI frameworks like Llama.cpp to run at near-native speed without rewriting code It is written in Rust Current support extends to Blender rendering and 32-bit PhysX games, while PyTorch compatibility remains actively under development by creator Andrzej Janik Despite losing corporate funding and surviving repository takedowns, ZLUDA offers developers an effective alternative to NVIDIA proprietary hardware lock-in The project lowers deployment costs for machine learning workloads by turning budget-friendly AMD GPUs into viable choices for running CUDA code Pi on a RTX 3060 12GB Pi is a lightweight coding-agent harness for local models https://pi.dev - https://github.com/earendil-works/pi https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nm4r-6XqEcM prefill speed (time to first output token) vs token-per-second generation MoE and grouped-query attention can reduce VRAM and KV-cache pressure Many llama.cpp guides are outdated; correct flags and tool settings are critical Small, focused toolsets can make local agents feel much faster and cleaner Local setups win on privacy and control, but still lose on hardest long-horizon tasks.

slides.title: Rust Is Winning Rust’s quiet systems takeover CISA
slides.text: Rust Is Winning Rust’s quiet systems takeover CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency) set a non-binding Jan 1, 2026 memory-safety roadmap deadline for C/C++ vendors OMB memo M-26-05 - shifting to “risk-based” agency discretion instead Meanwhile Rust adoption surged on its own: performance-driven rewrites like Cloudflare’s Pingora proxy and Discord’s latency-critical services https://blog.cloudflare.com/how-we-built-pingora-the-proxy-that-connects-cloudflare-to-the-internet/ https://github.com/cloudflare/pingora Google cut Android memory safety bugs from roughly 75% to under 20% by writing new systems code in Rust while leaving old C/C++ largely intact Linux, Android, major cloud vendors, and JavaScript tooling now embed Rust as a hard dependency, making it a practical requirement in modern systems stacks. DARPA and others explore AI-assisted C-to-Rust migration, underscoring a decade-scale transition rather than a sudden flip

slides.title: Zero Day Clock https://zerodayclock.com https://zerodayclock.com/collapse https://zerodayclock.com/audit https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/2024-zero-day-trends ZeroDayClock
slides.text: Zero Day Clock https://zerodayclock.com https://zerodayclock.com/collapse https://zerodayclock.com/audit https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/2024-zero-day-trends ZeroDayClock tracks the shrinking time from CVE disclosure to first confirmed exploitation across thousands of exploited CVEs ( CVE stands for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures ) The main trend is a rapid collapse in median time-to-exploit, from years to days, then hours, with zero-day exploitation now occurring on or before disclosure The exploit survival curves also shift left year over year, showing attackers are moving faster than patch cycles . The site argues this is an exponential decay, not a temporary dip GTIG’s 2024 analysis supports the broader pattern: zero-day exploitation remains elevated, and enterprise technologies are taking a larger share of attacks The practical takeaway is that patching alone is increasingly too slow ; exposure reduction and faster remediation matter more .
